docs.title: MT4Account (MRPC)
docs.text:
AccountSummaryData summary = account.accountSummary();
System.out.printf("%d %s: balance %s %s, equity %s, credit %s, leverage 1:%d%n", summary.getAccountLogin(),
        summary.getAccountUserName(), summary.getAccountBalance(), summary.getAccountCurrency(),
        summary.getAccountEquity(), summary.getAccountCredit(), summary.getAccountLeverage());

MT4's AccountSummary has no margin values. They come with the OnOpenedOrdersProfit stream (SubscriptionServiceGrpc): its account_info has margin, free_margin and margin_level, every timer_period_milliseconds. Open orders and history: OpenedOrders and OrdersHistory of AccountHelperGrpc, through account.authorized(AccountHelperGrpc.newBlockingStub(account.getChannel())).

docs.title: MT4Client (MT4 server protocol, no MRPC)
docs.text:
MT4Client is a different client. It speaks the MT4 server protocol straight to a broker's MT4 server (the broker's access point host and port), without MRPC and without an API key. It cannot connect to mt4.mrpc.pro; for the MRPC API use MT4Account.

MT4Client keeps the account, the open orders and the closed trades it receives from the MT4 server.

docs.title: Viewing Open Positions & Orders
docs.text:
The client keeps an in-memory concurrent map of open positions and orders:

import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.messages.res.OrderUpdateEvent;

ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, OrderUpdateEvent> openOrders = client.getOpenOrders();

for (OrderUpdateEvent order : openOrders.values()) {
    System.out.printf("Ticket #%d | Symbol: %s | Lots: %.2f | Type: %s | Open: %.5f | Profit: %.2f%n",
            order.ticket,
            order.symbol,
            order.lots / 100.0,
            order.orderType,
            order.openPrice,
            order.profit);
}

docs.title: Downloading Closed Order History
docs.text:
You can download closed trades over a specific time window:

import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.messages.res.OrderHistoryRes;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.parts.TradeRecord;

int oneYearAgo = (int) Instant.now().minus(365, ChronoUnit.DAYS).getEpochSecond();
int oneMonthAhead = (int) Instant.now().plus(30, ChronoUnit.DAYS).getEpochSecond();

OrderHistoryRes history = client.requestOrderHistory(oneYearAgo, oneMonthAhead);

for (TradeRecord trade : history.trades) {
    System.out.printf("History Ticket #%d: %s | Profit: %.2f | Closed at: %s%n",
            trade.ticket,
            trade.symbol,
            trade.profit,
            Instant.ofEpochSecond(trade.closeTime));
}

docs.title: MT4Account (the MRPC API)
docs.text:
The client of the MRPC MT4 API (mt4.mrpc.pro:443, gRPC over TLS). Every method returns the reply's data or throws MrpcException (getCode() is the API's error code, e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, or the gRPC status of a failed call).

public class MT4Account implements AutoCloseable {
    public MT4Account(String apiKey);                              // mt4.mrpc.pro:443
    public MT4Account(String grpcServer, String apiKey);           // host:port, TLS
    public MT4Account(ManagedChannel channel, String apiKey);      // your own channel

    public String connect(long user, String password, String serverName, int timeoutSeconds);  // ConnectEx, e.g. "TeleTrade-Demo"
    public String connect(long user, String password, String host, int port, int timeoutSeconds); // Connect by address
    public String getId(long user, String password);              // GetId; a following connect() uses this id
    public void attach(String terminalId);                        // an already connected terminal
    public String getTerminalId();

    public AccountSummaryData accountSummary();
    public QuoteData quote(String symbol);
    public OrderSendData orderSend(OrderSendRequest request);
    public OrderSendData orderSend(String symbol, OrderSendOperationType type, double lots);
    public OrderCloseDeleteData orderClose(int ticket);           // close a market order, delete a pending one
    public Subscription onSymbolTick(List<String> symbols, Consumer<OnSymbolMqlTickInfo> onTick, Consumer<Throwable> onError);

    public void disconnect(boolean delete);
    public void close();                                          // shuts the channel down

    public ManagedChannel getChannel();
    public <S extends AbstractStub<S>> S authorized(S stub);      // any generated stub, with the API key and terminal id
}

Every other method of the API is in the generated stubs (mt4_term_api.*Grpc), for example account.authorized(AccountHelperGrpc.newBlockingStub(account.getChannel())).openedOrders(...). Every method, its request and reply: API methods; try them at https://mt4.mrpc.pro/apiui.

public class MT4Client {

    public String getAccountCurrency();
    public String getCompany();

docs.title: MessageHandler
docs.text:
Callback interface of MT4Client for the events of the MT4 server connection.

public interface MessageHandler {
    void onConnected(MT4Client client);
    void onDisconnected(IOException exception, MT4Client client);
    void onMessage(MetaTraderMessage message, MT4Client client);
    void onReceiveFailure(DecoderException exception);
    void onSendFailure(Exception exception);
}

docs.title: MT4Account (MRPC)
docs.text:
MT4Account account = new MT4Account("your-api-key");            // mt4.mrpc.pro:443
String terminal = account.connect(7689280, "your-password", "TeleTrade-Demo", 120);

// ... calls ...

account.disconnect(false);   // true: stop the terminal and delete it
account.close();             // the channel

connect() returns once the terminal is connected and throws MrpcException when the server refuses (wrong password, unknown server, ...). connect(user, password, host, port, timeoutSeconds) connects by the address of the broker's MT4 server instead of its name.

There is no automatic reconnect: when a call throws TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND or the channel fails, call connect() again.

docs.title: API key and terminal id
docs.text:
• API key: from https://mrpc.pro/my (sign up free at https://mrpc.pro/signup). Pass it to new MT4Account(apiKey) or set MRPC_API_KEY; without one the client sends TRIAL.
  • Terminal id: connect() receives it from the server, keeps it (getTerminalId()) and sends it with every later call and stream. attach(id) uses a terminal that is already connected.

docs.title: Connection lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Your Application
    participant Client as MT4Client
    participant Server as MT4 Server

    App->>Client: new MT4Client(host, port, handler)
    App->>Client: client.connect(login, password)
    Client->>Server: TCP Connect & Handshake
    Server-->>Client: Challenge Key
    Client->>Server: Encrypted Credentials
    Server-->>Client: Login OK & Symbols Table
    Client-->>App: handler.onConnected(client)

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
Instantiate MT4Client with the host and port of the broker's MT4 server and a MessageHandler:

MT4Client client = new MT4Client("<broker MT4 server host>", 443, new MessageHandler() {
    @Override
    public void onConnected(MT4Client client) {
        System.out.println("Session connected and authenticated.");
    }

    @Override
    public void onMessage(MetaTraderMessage message, MT4Client client) {
        // Handle incoming messages
    }

    @Override
    public void onDisconnected(IOException exception, MT4Client client) {
        System.err.println("Session terminated: " + exception.getMessage());
    }

    @Override
    public void onReceiveFailure(DecoderException e) {
        System.err.println("Decoder failure: " + e.getMessage());
    }

    @Override
    public void onSendFailure(Exception e) {
        System.err.println("Send failed: " + e.getMessage());
    }
});

// Start asynchronous connection
client.connect(1002345, "investor_or_master_password");

docs.title: Connection state
docs.text:
You can query connection state anytime:

// Check if initial handshake and base account synchronization is finished
if (client.isBaseAccountRead()) {
    System.out.println("Ready to send trading operations!");
}

// Server build info
int build = client.getLoginHelper().getServerBuild();
System.out.println("Server MT4 build version: " + build);

docs.text:

docs.title: MT4Account (MRPC)
docs.text:
QuoteData quote = account.quote("EURUSD");
System.out.println("EURUSD " + quote.getBid() + " / " + quote.getAsk());

try (MT4Account.Subscription ticks = account.onSymbolTick(List.of("EURUSD", "GBPUSD"),
        tick -> System.out.println(tick.getSymbol() + " " + tick.getBid() + " / " + tick.getAsk()),
        error -> System.err.println("stream error: " + error.getMessage()))) {
    Thread.sleep(10_000);
}   // close() ends the stream

onError gets an error the stream answers with (an MrpcException, e.g. NO_CHARTS_OPENED_FOR_SYMBOLS for a symbol the terminal doesn't have) or the stream's failure. Bars: Bars of QuoteHistoryGrpc (or QuoteHistory of MarketInfoGrpc), through account.authorized(...).

docs.title: Subscribing to Live Quotes
docs.text:
To receive live tick updates, request quotes using the symbol code from the client's SymbolTable:

// Resolve symbol code
short eurusdCode = client.getSymbolTable().getCode("EURUSD");
short gbpusdCode = client.getSymbolTable().getCode("GBPUSD");

SubscribeQuotesReq req = new SubscribeQuotesReq();
req.symbolCodes = new short[]{ eurusdCode, gbpusdCode };
client.sendRequestAsync(req);

docs.title: Handling Incoming Quotes
docs.text:
In your MessageHandler:

@Override
public void onMessage(MetaTraderMessage message, MT4Client c) {
    if (message instanceof QuoteEvent quote) {
        System.out.printf("[%s] Bid: %.5f | Ask: %.5f | Time: %s%n",
                quote.symbol,
                quote.bid,
                quote.ask,
                java.time.Instant.ofEpochSecond(quote.time));
    }
}

docs.title: Unsubscribing from Quotes
docs.text:
To cancel active subscriptions, send an empty symbol code array:

SubscribeQuotesReq unsubReq = new SubscribeQuotesReq();
unsubReq.symbolCodes = new short[0];
client.sendRequestAsync(unsubReq);

docs.title: Requesting Historical Bars
docs.text:
You can query historical OHLCV candlestick data across any timeframe:

import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.enums.Timeframe;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.messages.req.HistoricalBarsReq;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.messages.res.HistoricalBarsRes;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.parts.BarRecord;

HistoricalBarsReq req = new HistoricalBarsReq();
req.symbol = "EURUSD";
req.timeframe = Timeframe.H1; // M1, M5, M15, M30, H1, H4, D1, W1, MN1
req.fromTime = (int) (System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000 - (7 * 86400)); // 7 days ago
req.count = 100;

HistoricalBarsRes res = (HistoricalBarsRes) client.sendRequest(req);

int digits = client.getSymbolTable().getDigits("EURUSD");
double point = Math.pow(10, -digits);

for (BarRecord bar : res.bars) {
    double open = bar.open * point;
    double high = bar.high * point;
    double low = bar.low * point;
    double close = bar.close * point;
    System.out.printf("Time: %s | Open: %.5f | High: %.5f | Low: %.5f | Close: %.5f | Vol: %.0f%n",
            java.time.Instant.ofEpochSecond(bar.time), open, high, low, close, bar.volume);
}

docs.title: MT4Account (MRPC)
docs.text:
OrderSendData order = account.orderSend("EURUSD", OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, 0.01);
System.out.println("Ticket #" + order.getTicket() + " at " + order.getPrice());

// pending order with stops
OrderSendData pending = account.orderSend(OrderSendRequest.newBuilder()
        .setSymbol("EURUSD").setOperationType(OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUYLIMIT)
        .setVolume(0.01).setPrice(1.05).setStoploss(1.04).setTakeprofit(1.07).build());

account.orderClose(order.getTicket());      // closes the market order
account.orderClose(pending.getTicket());    // deletes the pending one

An order the server refuses throws MrpcException with the server's code. Modifying an order: OrderModify of TradingHelperGrpc, through account.authorized(TradingHelperGrpc.newBlockingStub(account.getChannel())).

docs.title: Opening an Order
docs.text:
MetaTrader 4 brokers use either Market Execution or Instant Execution. You can check the execution mode using SymbolInfo:

import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.enums.Execution;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.enums.Op;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.enums.TradeCommand;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.messages.req.OrderTransactionReq;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.messages.res.TradeEvent;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.network.parts.SymbolInfo;

SymbolInfo symbolInfo = client.getSymbolTable().getInfo("EURUSD");
boolean isMarket = symbolInfo.execution == Execution.Market;

OrderTransactionReq req = new OrderTransactionReq();
req.orderType = Op.Buy;       // Op.Buy or Op.Sell
req.symbol = "EURUSD";
req.lots = 10;                // 10 = 0.10 lots (lots are in hundredths)
req.comment = "AlgoOrder";

if (isMarket) {
    req.tradeCommand = TradeCommand.Market;
    req.price = 0;
    req.slippage = 0;
} else {
    req.tradeCommand = TradeCommand.Instant;
    req.price = latestQuote.ask;
    req.slippage = 30; // 3 pips
}

TradeEvent result = (TradeEvent) client.sendRequest(req);
if (result.ticket > 0) {
    System.out.println("Order opened successfully! Ticket: #" + result.ticket);
} else {
    System.err.println("Order failed with error code: " + result.errorCode);
}

docs.title: Modifying Stop Loss and Take Profit
docs.text:
OrderTransactionReq modifyReq = new OrderTransactionReq();
modifyReq.tradeCommand = TradeCommand.Modify;
modifyReq.orderType = Op.Buy;
modifyReq.symbol = "EURUSD";
modifyReq.ticket = ticket;
modifyReq.price = openPrice;
modifyReq.stopLoss = openPrice - 0.0050;   // 50 pips SL
modifyReq.takeProfit = openPrice + 0.0050; // 50 pips TP

TradeEvent modifyRes = (TradeEvent) client.sendRequest(modifyReq);
if (modifyRes.ticket > 0) {
    System.out.println("Order modified successfully!");
}

docs.title: Closing an Order
docs.text:
OrderTransactionReq closeReq = new OrderTransactionReq();
closeReq.orderType = Op.Buy;
closeReq.symbol = "EURUSD";
closeReq.ticket = ticket;
closeReq.lots = 10; // Lots to close

if (isMarket) {
    closeReq.tradeCommand = TradeCommand.CloseMarket;
    closeReq.price = 0;
    closeReq.slippage = 0;
} else {
    closeReq.tradeCommand = TradeCommand.CloseInstant;
    closeReq.price = latestQuote.bid;
    closeReq.slippage = 30;
}

TradeEvent closeRes = (TradeEvent) client.sendRequest(closeReq);
System.out.println("Closed order ticket #" + closeRes.ticket);

pendingReq.lots = 10;
pendingReq.price = targetLimitPrice;
pendingReq.stopLoss = stopLossPrice;
pendingReq.takeProfit = takeProfitPrice;

Information, never converted. 0 while the account is not connected yet. server_utc_offset_seconds getServerUtcOffsetSeconds() int32 The broker server's offset from UTC in seconds, positive = ahead of UTC: validated by the terminal (a multiple of 15 minutes). Information, never converted; it is the offset behind every *_utc field of this API. ABSENT (has_server_utc_offset_seconds is false) while it is not known yet: the account is not connected, or it is connected but the market is closed and no price quote has arrived since the terminal started - MT4 learns the offset from a live quote. Absent never means UTC+0 (a UTC+0 broker sends 0 and has it present). The *_utc fields stay unset until it is known. docs.title: API methods
docs.text: Every public method of the MT4 API, generated from the protos this package is built from. Each is a gRPC method of package mt4_term_api on mt4.mrpc.pro:443 and a REST route on https://mt4.mrpc.pro (server streams also as a WebSocket on the same path, wss://mt4.mrpc.pro/...?id=...&apikey=...). Every reply carries either data (described below) or error (see Errors). Try them in the browser: https://mt4.mrpc.pro/apiui.

docs.title: Calling a method
docs.text:
Every method below is a method of the generated stub of its service (mt4_term_api.{Service}Grpc). Get it with the API key and terminal id from your MT4Account:

var marketInfo = account.authorized(MarketInfoGrpc.newBlockingStub(account.getChannel()));
var reply = marketInfo.quote(QuoteRequest.newBuilder().setSymbol("EURUSD").build());
if (reply.hasError()) throw new IllegalStateException(reply.getError().getErrorMessage());
System.out.println(reply.getData().getBid() + " / " + reply.getData().getAsk());

Field foo_bar is getFooBar() / setFooBar(value) on the builder; a repeated field is getFooBarList() / addFooBar(value) / addAllFooBar(list). A server stream is a blocking stub's Iterator or an async stub (newStub) with a StreamObserver.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text: ============================================================================ Accounts: the MT4 accounts (terminals) that belong to your API key. This is the call to make when you need the terminal ids of accounts that already exist - started from the dashboard or by an earlier ConnectEx - so that you can send them as the "id" header of every other call. Unlike the terminal calls it needs NO "id" header: it is answered from the platform's records of the API key sent in the "APIKey" header, and it never starts, wakes or bills a terminal. Accounts are listed newest first (by started_utc, then terminal_id) and returned by page. Only accounts of THIS platform's endpoint are listed (mt5.mrpc.pro lists MT5 accounts, mt4.mrpc.pro lists MT4 accounts). ============================================================================

docs.title: Accounts.List
docs.text:
Lists the accounts of the API key sent in the APIKey header, one page per call. Pass the next_page_token of a page back as page_token to continue; an empty next_page_token means that was the last page. [DefaultValues] { "includeStopped": "false", "pageSize": "200" }

  • gRPC: mt4_term_api.Accounts/List (unary)
  • REST: GET /Accounts

Request AccountsListRequest

Field Java Type Description state getState() string Only accounts in this state, e.g. "Connected", "Syncing", "Unreachable", "WrongPassword", "Suspended" (the vocabulary of ConnectState.state, compared without regard to case). Empty = every state. login getLogin() uint64 Only the account with this login number. 0 = every login. include_stopped getIncludeStopped() bool false (default): only accounts that are queued, starting or running, or that stopped on their own (Unreachable, WrongPassword, Suspended, Expired) and can be started again. true: also accounts that were stopped by the user, by an API call or by an administrator. Deleted accounts are never listed. page_size getPageSize() int32 Accounts per page, 1..1000. 0 = 200. A larger value is clamped, a negative one is rejected with ACCOUNTS_PAGE_SIZE_INVALID. page_token getPageToken() string The next_page_token of the previous page; empty for the first page. Must be sent with the same state, login and include_stopped. Undecodable -> ACCOUNTS_PAGE_TOKEN_INVALID.

Reply data AccountsListData

docs.title: QuoteHistory
docs.text: ============================================================================ Quote history: the bars a chart is drawn from, for one symbol - returned by PAGE, oldest first. MetaTrader 4 keeps no tick history, so there is no Ticks call here; the MT5 API has one. Bars walks a time range forward. A page carries at most page_size bars and, when the range holds more, a next_page_token; passing that token back (same symbol, timeframe and range) returns the next page. An empty next_page_token means the range is exhausted. Tokens are opaque: a client stores and returns them, nothing else. History lives in the terminal and is fetched from the broker on demand. The first request for a symbol or a period the terminal has not loaded yet can take a few seconds, and when the broker has not delivered it within that time the call answers with an error whose error_code is QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY - ask again a moment later. Every call needs the terminal id header ("id"), like every other call. ============================================================================

A time before the broker's first bar is clamped to that first bar. from_time_utc getFromTimeUtc() int64 from_time in UTC: send either from_time or from_time_utc, not both. to_time getToTime() int64 Unix seconds (UTC) of the newest bar wanted, inclusive. 0 = now. to_time_utc getToTimeUtc() int64 to_time in UTC: send either to_time or to_time_utc, not both. page_size getPageSize() int32 Bars per page, 1..5000. 0 = 1000. page_token getPageToken() string The next_page_token of the previous page, to continue; empty for the first page. docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every reply of the API carries either data or error; a refused request is an answer like any other (HTTP 200 on REST), not a failed call.

Every method of MT4Account returns what the server answered or throws an MrpcException:

  • the API answered with an error: getCode() is the error code, getError() the reply's whole Error (the fields below);
  • the call failed (network, deadline, server down): getCode() is the gRPC status (UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, ...) and getError() is null.

With the generated stubs you get the reply itself: reply.hasError() instead of reply.hasData().

docs.title: A refused order
docs.text:
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MrpcException;

// account: a connected MT4Account
try {
    account.orderSend("EURUSD", OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, 0.001);
} catch (MrpcException e) {
    if (e.getError() != null) {                                     // the API answered with an error
        System.out.println(e.getCode());                            // MQL4_EXECUTION_FAILED
        System.out.println(e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode());      // 131 (invalid trade volume)
        System.out.println(e.getError().getMqlErrorDescription());  // invalid trade volume
    } else {
        System.out.println("call failed: " + e.getCode());          // the gRPC status, e.g. UNAVAILABLE
    }
}

When the broker or the terminal refuses a trade request, the MT4 error is in mql_error_int_code / mql_error_code (MqlErrorCode: 131 invalid trade volume, 134 not enough money, 4220 symbol select error, ...), the error type is MQL_EXECUTION and error_code is MQL4_EXECUTION_FAILED.

docs.title: The error
docs.text:
Error has:

Field error_code what went wrong, e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND; use it in your code error_message the same for people, with details type where it happened (ErrorType): MRPC, MRPC_VALIDATION, MRPC_TIMEOUT, MQL_EXECUTION, ... mql_error_code, mql_error_int_code, mql_error_description the MQL error of the terminal, when the terminal refused (MqlErrorCode) command_type_name the terminal command that failed

docs.title: Codes you will meet
docs.text:
error_code Meaning What to do TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND the terminal id is not a running terminal (never was, or stopped) connect again MQL4_EXECUTION_FAILED the terminal refused the request: see the MQL fields fix the request (volume, price, stops, ...) NO_CHARTS_OPENED_FOR_SYMBOLS a tick stream for symbols the terminal does not have check the symbol names

The codes of the limits (calls per minute, the order queue, tick streams) and of the API key: Errors & Limits.

docs.title: Getting Started with JavaMT4
docs.text: Quick Setup & Overview - Connect to MetaTrader 4 from Java in a few minutes.

docs.title: What is JavaMT4?
docs.text:
JavaMT4 is the Java client of the MRPC MT4 API (mt4.mrpc.pro:443, gRPC over TLS):

  • MT4Account: connect, account, quotes, orders, tick stream, disconnect (see API Reference).
  • The generated gRPC stubs of the whole API (mt4_term_api.*Grpc), for everything else, with account.authorized(stub) adding the API key and terminal id.

The package also has MT4Client, a client of the MT4 server protocol that connects straight to a broker's MT4 server (no MRPC). The other pages of these guides describe the API itself (methods, enums, return codes, streams); some of their code samples are in Python, the calls and messages are the same from Java.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Gradle, from JitPack (built from this repository on request):

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
    maven { url 'https://jitpack.io' }
}
dependencies {
    implementation 'com.github.MetaRPC:JavaMT4:fa9acfb453'   // a commit of this repository; main-SNAPSHOT = the latest
}

Maven: add the repository https://jitpack.io and the dependency com.github.MetaRPC / JavaMT4 / fa9acfb453. The jar brings gRPC and the generated mt4_term_api stubs along; Java 17+. It is not on Maven Central.

Or build it yourself: git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/JavaMT4.git && cd JavaMT4 && ./gradlew publishToMavenLocal installs pro.mrpc:mt4:1.0.0 into your local Maven repository (mavenLocal()).

docs.title: API key
docs.text:
1. Sign up free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Create a key at https://mrpc.pro/my under API Keys.
  3. Pass it to new MT4Account(apiKey) or set MRPC_API_KEY.

docs.title: API key and terminal id
docs.text:
• API key: from https://mrpc.pro/my (sign up free at https://mrpc.pro/signup). Pass it to new MT4Account(apiKey) or set MRPC_API_KEY; without one the client sends TRIAL.
  • Terminal id: connect() receives it from the server, keeps it (getTerminalId()) and sends it with every later call and stream. attach(id) uses a terminal that is already connected.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiAccountHelper.AccountSummaryData;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendData;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Account;

public class App {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        try (MT4Account account = new MT4Account(System.getenv("MRPC_API_KEY"))) {      // mt4.mrpc.pro:443
            account.connect(Long.parseLong(System.getenv("MT4_LOGIN")), System.getenv("MT4_PASSWORD"), "TeleTrade-Demo", 120);
            try {
                AccountSummaryData summary = account.accountSummary();
                System.out.println("Balance: " + summary.getAccountBalance() + " " + summary.getAccountCurrency());

                OrderSendData order = account.orderSend("EURUSD", OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, 0.01);
                System.out.println("Ticket #" + order.getTicket() + " at " + order.getPrice());
            } finally {
                account.disconnect(false);   // true also deletes the terminal
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Streams
docs.text:
The API pushes data over gRPC server streams. Ticks have their own method in the client: account.onSymbolTick(symbols, onTick, onError). Every other stream is a method of SubscriptionServiceGrpc:

Stream What it sends OnSymbolTick ticks of the symbols OnTrade every change of orders, with the account values OnOpenedOrdersProfit the profit of the open orders and the account values (with margin), every timer_period_milliseconds OnOpenedOrdersTickets the tickets of the open orders, every pull_interval_milliseconds OnConnectState the state of your terminals (Connected, Unreachable, Stopped, ...) OnJournal, OnExperts the terminal's journal and Experts log (a new stream starts with what is already written)

Their requests and messages: API methods.

docs.title: Using a stream
docs.text:
OnOpenedOrdersProfit, the account's equity, margin and profit every second:

import io.grpc.Context;
import io.grpc.Status;
import io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiSubscriptions.OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiSubscriptions.OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest;
import mt4_term_api.SubscriptionServiceGrpc;

// account: a connected MT4Account
var subscriptions = account.authorized(SubscriptionServiceGrpc.newStub(account.getChannel()));
var request = OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest.newBuilder().setTimerPeriodMilliseconds(1000).build();

Context.CancellableContext stream = Context.current().withCancellation();
stream.run(() -> subscriptions.onOpenedOrdersProfit(request, new StreamObserver<OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply>() {
    @Override
    public void onNext(OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply reply) {
        if (reply.hasError()) {                                   // the API answered with an error
            System.err.println("stream error: " + reply.getError().getErrorCode());
            return;
        }
        if (!reply.hasData()) return;                             // a heartbeat (after 30 s without data)
        var info = reply.getData().getAccountInfo();
        System.out.println("equity " + info.getEquity() + ", margin " + info.getMargin() + ", profit " + info.getProfit());
    }

    @Override
    public void onError(Throwable t) {
        if (Status.fromThrowable(t).getCode() == Status.Code.CANCELLED) return;   // stream.cancel()
        System.err.println("stream failed: " + t.getMessage());                    // open it again
    }

    @Override
    public void onCompleted() {
    }
}));

// ... when done
stream.cancel(null);
  • Every message has data or error. A message with neither is a heartbeat: after 30 seconds without data the server sends one so that proxies keep the connection open. Skip it.
  • An error message reports a problem with the stream's request (for example NO_CHARTS_OPENED_FOR_SYMBOLS for a symbol the terminal does not have); the stream may end after it.
  • stream.cancel(null) ends it (onError then gets CANCELLED, which is not a failure).
  • A stream does not resume by itself. When it fails or ends while you still need it, open it again; when calls answer TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, the terminal is gone: connect first.
  • Opening a stream counts as a call toward the per-terminal limits, the messages it delivers do not; the number of tick streams per terminal is limited too: Errors & Limits.

docs.title: In a browser
docs.text: Browsers cannot speak gRPC to the API (no gRPC-Web is served). Every stream is also a WebSocket on its REST path, with the terminal id and key in the query: wss://mt4.mrpc.pro/OnOpenedOrdersProfit?id=<terminal id>&apikey=<key>&timerPeriodMilliseconds=1000. See the client guide.
